# COP32 guide app — design system v1.0

**Date:** 2026-11-16. **Applies to:** the native app in `app/`, version 0.9.0. **Decisions behind it:** D73 (direction "Daylight"), D74 (English first, no cultural motifs), D75 (typefaces), D76 (Home is general), D77 (soft, deep green, no rules), D78 (Home without a hero photograph), D79 (raised blocks, floating tab bar).
**Machine-readable source:** `tokens.json`, generated by `build_tokens.py`, which also writes the app's theme file and fails if any colour pair misses its contrast target (80 pairs, 0 failures). No colour or size is typed by hand into a component.
**Earlier versions and the web prototype's rules:** `design-system-history.md`.

**What this document is not.** It is a record of rules the app follows, checked in a browser render of the app's own code. It has **not** been validated with users, with a screen reader on a phone, or across a range of devices. The founder has reviewed versions up to 0.7.0 on one phone; 0.8.0 and 0.9.0 have not been seen on a phone at the time of writing.

## 1. Identity and honesty
- The app is independent and says so: on the first-run screen, in one permanent line on Home, and in About. It uses no government, UN or official COP32 emblem (D65, D66).
- Name, mark and palette come from one brand configuration (`app/src/theme/brand.ts`). Two brands ship: "COP32" and an invented "Your Event", switchable in Settings to show that the identity can change in a day.
- The palette, mark and typefaces are original to this project. The kinds of component (floating bar, shadowed cards, icon tiles) follow what host-country apps do, in particular the COP31 app; none of that app's artwork, colours, typeface or photographs is used (D67 as narrowed by D79).
- Photographs are openly licensed, credited in the app (About) and in `image-credits.md`. They illustrate themes; they do not show COP32 or its venue, and some were taken outside Ethiopia.

## 2. Principles
1. **One focal point per screen.** A status card, a title, or the next session — never several things of equal weight.
2. **Content sits in blocks.** White raised blocks on a tinted page. No rules, hairlines or outlines.
3. **Colour means something.** Deep green = go, selected, brand. Amber = save and "now". Red = emergency or delete. Soft green = secondary.
4. **Honest states.** "To be confirmed" is a designed state. Empty lists say what will appear and from whom. Nothing invented is presented as fact.
5. **Works for everyone.** Text to 200%, 48 px targets, contrast checked on every build, motion removable.
6. **Offline is a mark of quality**, shown as a green "Saved offline" pill, not as an apology.

## 3. Colour
| Role | Light | Dark | Used for |
|---|---|---|---|
| Page (`bg`) | `#EDF3F0` | `#09110F` | The background of every screen; wells inside a block |
| Block (`surface`) | `#FFFFFF` | `#16231F` | Cards, row groups, chips, round buttons, the tab bar |
| Well (`surfaceAlt`) | `#DDE8E3` | `#21322C` | Tags, skeletons, ended states |
| Text | `#10231E` | `#F1EEE6` | Body and titles |
| Secondary text | `#465650` | `#A8B3AC` | Second lines, meta |
| Tertiary text | `#586862` | `#96A29B` | Footnotes, ended items |
| Deep green (`ink`, `primary`) | `#0B4F47` | `#A9E0D5` / `#8FD3C8` | Main buttons, selected states, links, the tab disc |
| Soft green (`primarySoft`) | `#DCEDE7` | `#173A35` | Icon discs, secondary buttons; large green fills in the dark theme |
| Amber (`accent`) | `#F29F3D` | `#F29F3D` | Save, the "now" marker, the arrow on featured cards |
| Success | `#1F5E12` on `#E3F2DA` | `#9FE0A8` on `#17301C` | "Saved offline", "Open to public" |
| Danger | `#B3261E` on `#FCE7E3` | `#FF9D92` on `#3A1A16` | Emergency, live, delete |

In the dark theme large green fills (status card, emergency card, quick tiles) use the deep soft green with pale text; only small selected controls use the bright green.

## 4. Type (D75)
- **Bricolage Grotesque** 600/700/800 — titles and clock times. **Instrument Sans** 400/500/600/700 — everything else. **Noto Sans Ethiopic** — any text containing Ge'ez, chosen automatically per string. All are open-licence and bundled; nothing is fetched at run time.
- Scale (px): display 36 · large title 32 · clock 30 · title1 28 · display small 24 · title2 22 · title3 19 · headline and body 17 · then callout, subhead, footnote, caption and label below that (exact values in `tokens.json`).
- The user's text-size choice (100–200%) scales everything. The largest styles stop at 135%; labels under icons and the tab-bar labels are sized from their column instead.

## 5. Space, shape, shadow
- Page margin 20 px. Spacing steps 2, 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 32, 40, 48, 64. Content is capped at 720 px wide and centred.
- Corners: 12 small, 20 medium, 24 image cards and tiles, 28 panels and sheets, fully round for pills and discs.
- **Shadow has three levels** (`app/src/ui/lift.ts`): 1 for small controls (chips, round buttons, search), 2 for cards and row groups, 3 for the tab bar, the status card and featured photographs. Green-tinted in the light theme, black in the dark. **Not drawn on Android before version 9**; there the white block on the tinted page does the separating alone.

## 6. Components
| Component | Rule |
|---|---|
| **Header (tab roots)** | Mark and name left; three 44 px round white buttons right: search, Emergency (red, always one tap away, D44), profile. Same on every tab. |
| **Sub-header** | Round back or close button, then an optional short title. |
| **Screen title** | One style everywhere: display face, with an optional line of supporting text and the "Saved offline" pill on tab roots. |
| **Section title** | Title2, optional single link on the right. No rule under it. |
| **Button** | A 54 px pill. Amber = save (once per screen at most). Deep green = the main way forward. Soft green = secondary. Text only = minor. Red = delete. |
| **Chip** | 40 px white pill inside a 48 px target; selected = deep green. Chips scroll or wrap; never cut mid-word. |
| **Day tiles / segmented control** | Equal white tiles; selected = deep green. Days carry a small "DAY" caption over a large number. |
| **Row group** | Rows that belong together share one white block. A row: a 44 px soft-green disc with an icon, or two initials for a person or organisation; title; optional second line; optional value; a chevron if it navigates. Emergency rows use a red-tinted disc. |
| **Session card** | Top line: clock, time range, live or ended tag, bookmark. Then format and access in green, the title, and a last line with the room on a soft chip and a 38 px round arrow (grey when ended). |
| **Status card (Home)** | Deep green, 28 px corners, shadow 3: small capital label, "Saved offline" pill, title, one honest status line linking to Sources and status. On a conference-day preview: day, time and an amber progress bar. |
| **Featured carousel** | One photograph per screen width, 236 px tall (330 from 150% text), snapping, page dots. The title sits on a solid deep-green plate inset 10 px, with a 40 px amber arrow disc. |
| **Quick-action tile** | 122 × 104 px deep-green tile: white icon top-left, label bottom-left, the same icon large and faint off the bottom-right corner. In a scrolling row. |
| **Image card** | Photograph across the top of a white block. On Visit a white icon disc overlaps the photograph's lower edge. |
| **Tag** | Small capsule with an icon and words: live, next, open to public, restricted, ended. Colour is never the only signal. |
| **Notice** | Soft tinted panel with icon, title and text; four tones. "Danger" is announced immediately to screen readers. |
| **Empty or unavailable state** | An icon disc, what the situation is, and what still works. Never "something went wrong". |
| **Sheet** | Slides up from the bottom over a dimmed page; 28 px top corners; a close button; actions at the bottom. |
| **Tab bar** | A white bar 66 px tall with fully rounded ends, inset 12 px from the screen edges, shadow 3. One 54 px deep-green disc stands 16 px above the bar over the selected tab; the selected icon sits on it in white; its label below is green and bold. Labels are sized from the column so the longest ("Programme") always fits. |

## 7. Imagery and icons
- Words are never set directly on a photograph. Where a title sits over an image it is on a solid plate; every control over a photograph has a solid backing.
- Photographs appear on: the featured carousel, session pages, Visit guide cards and pages, explainers, exhibitor pages. Nine images, about 1024 px wide — they may look soft on a large phone.
- Icons are Lucide outlines (ISC licence), bundled. Stroke 1.8–2 at rest, 2.2 when selected or inside a button. The saved bookmark is the only filled icon.

## 8. Motion
- Entrances: 240 ms with a short rise, items 40 ms apart, capped at 280 ms. Press: scale to 0.97.
- **Save**: the bookmark fills and overshoots once, with a single haptic tick. This is the one celebratory animation.
- **Tab change**: the disc slides to the tapped tab on a spring and stretches about 28% sideways for a moment; the icon rises 15 px onto it.
- Sheets slide up. The featured carousel snaps.
- "Reduce motion" in Settings removes all of it; positions change at once.
- **Not built:** a shared-element transition from a session card to its page.

## 9. Accessibility rules the build enforces or the code follows
- Contrast: every text and icon pair at WCAG 2.2 AA, computed from the tokens on each build.
- Targets: 48 px minimum for every control.
- Text: scales to 200% at 320 px wide with no sideways scrolling. From 130% trailing values move under titles; from 150% the featured card grows and tiles enlarge.
- Each control has a spoken label; rows read as one item; selected and saved states are announced; decorative images and the page dots are hidden from screen readers.
- Ended sessions step back through colour roles that still pass contrast, never through transparency.
- Automated scan (axe-core) on every route in English and Amharic, light and dark: 108 runs, 0 violations — **in a browser**. A TalkBack run on a phone is still owed.

## 10. Languages
English first (D74). The app has Amharic strings and switches script and typeface correctly, but the Amharic text is an unreviewed draft and is labelled so in Settings. A proper edition needs native-speaking editors.

## 11. What still needs real-world validation
- The tab-bar animation, the shadows and touch feedback on real Android phones, including one older than Android 9.
- TalkBack, large text and dark mode on a phone.
- Whether the photographs are sharp enough on a large screen.
- Whether real users find things: the information architecture has only been tested by script.
- The Amharic edition.
